````text
1	# Harness: build spec
2	
3	**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.
4	
5	The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.
6	
7	## 1. Repos
8	
9	Two separate git repos, side by side:
10	
11	```
12	workspace/
13	  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
14	  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
15	```
16	
17	The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.
18	
19	```
20	harness/
21	  package.json              npm workspaces
22	  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
23	    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
24	    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
25	    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
26	    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
27	    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
28	    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
29	    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
30	    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
31	    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
32	    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
33	  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
34	    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
35	    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
36	    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
37	    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
38	    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
39	    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
40	    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
41	    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
42	  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
43	  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
44	```
45	
46	Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).
47	
48	## 2. Hard rules
49	
50	1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
51	2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
52	3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
53	4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.
54	
55	## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)
56	
57	Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.
58	
59	**Tests** are assigned to a domain by its `tests` globs. A test file counts as part of that domain for the rule checker's import rules and the footprint and is listed in the inspector, but it is not drawn in a cell and draws no edges. Tests may write any table: seeding fixture rows is setup, not a product write, so `owns_writes` skips them.
60	
61	**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`. It resolves relative paths by trying the specifier as written, then `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`, and maps a `.js` specifier to `.ts`. It ignores bare package and `node:` imports (Scout has none that matter).
62	
63	**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert(` and `db.update(` followed by a string literal in any quote style gives `{file, table}` pairs.
64	
65	## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites
66	
67	```ts
68	type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
69	function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
70	```
71	
72	`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:
73	
74	| Kind | Fires when |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
77	| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
78	| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |
79	
80	Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.
81	
82	The three call sites, all using the same function:
83	
84	1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
85	2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
86	3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).
87	
88	## 5. Events
89	
90	```ts
91	type HarnessEvent = {
92	  id: string; t: number;
93	  session: string;          // coding session id
94	  turn: string | null;
95	  kind:
96	    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
97	    | 'violation_found'
98	    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
99	    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
100	    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
101	    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
102	  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
103	  path?: string;
104	  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
105	};
106	```
107	
108	The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.
109	
110	## 6. The coding session
111	
112	One long-lived streaming session:
113	
114	```ts
115	query({
116	  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
117	  options: {
118	    cwd: REPO,
119	    permissionMode: 'plan',
120	    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
121	    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
122	    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
123	    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
124	    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
125	  },
126	});
127	```
128	
129	**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), every standing decision from `decisions/` (with the invariant it qualifies and the option it rejected), and these rules:
130	
131	> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.
132	
133	The brief does **not** list the seeded invariants (`source: cartographer`). They are enforced at plan and edit time instead. Stated up front, they would make the agent comply silently, so the user never sees the choice and nothing gets recorded. Once the user answers a fork, the resulting decision is in every later brief, and the next session follows it without asking. That contrast, asked once and then remembered, is the memory beat of the demo.
134	
135	**Turn flow:**
136	
137	1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
138	2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
139	3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
140	4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
141	5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
142	6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.
143	
144	**Hooks:**
145	
146	| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
147	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
148	| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
149	| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
150	| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
151	| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |
152	
153	**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.
154	
155	**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.
156	
157	## 7. Plan versus built
158	
159	- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
160	- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
161	- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
162	- **New versus existing violations:** a violation found on load is drawn red, with a badge on its cell counting the files involved. A violation raised by this turn's plan or edits must look different from the map before the turn, even when it repeats an existing one (on Scout, the 10-K plan copies `news-summarize.ts` into the same red cell and toward the same provider). Its ghost edge gets its own lane, offset from any solid edge between the same cells, and the cell gets a separate **new** badge naming the file.
163	
164	## 8. Design memory
165	
166	When a fork is answered:
167	
168	1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
169	2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). Commit both files and only those (`git commit -- domains.yaml decisions/DR-<n>.md`), so the coding session's uncommitted edits stay out of the commit.
170	3. Tell Claude, in the next tool result, to record it in Alike with `mcp__alike__record_decision`, giving it the exact arguments: `title`, `outcome`, `rationale` (including the rejected option), `decision_type: standing`, `status: made`, and one path anchor per governed file, `{ kind: path, label: governs, path, repository: owner/name }` (field names checked with `describe_entity_kind`, see VERIFY.md). Emit `decision_recorded` when the call succeeds.
171	
172	Memory is then used three ways:
173	
174	- **Provenance:** clicking an edge or cell shows the decisions and turns behind it ("added in turn 3, DR-4").
175	- **Session brief:** every standing decision goes into `brief()` for every new session (§6).
176	- **Rejected options stay rejected:** when a plan or edit hits an invariant that has a linked decision, the violation reason says "You decided this in DR-4: <title>," and the ledger counts it as a rejected option blocked.
177	
178	## 9. Time ledger and turn summary
179	
180	Counts only; minutes appear only in the pitch, taken from the baseline run (§12).
181	
182	| Counter | Definition |
183	| --- | --- |
184	| Lines changed | git `--numstat` added + removed, turn baseline → turn end |
185	| Cells to review | cells with a finding of severity 1–3 below |
186	| Forks caught before code | `plan_violation` events resolved before any `edited` event in the turn |
187	| Rejected options blocked | violations that cited an existing decision |
188	
189	Severity for the turn summary, loudest first: **1** invariant hit (red) · **2** new cross-domain edge or new external (amber, one glance) · **3** unplanned edit (amber) · **4** everything else in the plan (quiet).
190	
191	## 10. Load and the cartographer
192	
193	1. `repo_scanned`: full fact scan (§3).
194	2. If `domains.yaml` is missing, run the **cartographer**: a separate one-shot `query()` with read-only tools, a smaller model, and `outputFormat` set to the `domains.yaml` JSON schema. Input: the file tree, the import edges and the table writes. Ask it for 5–9 domains in product language, layers suited to the repo, and invariants it can infer from the facts (sole importers of a vendor, sole writers of a table, absent edges). → `map_proposed`.
195	3. The shell plays the map assembling (`file_assigned` events, staggered about 15 ms apart) and shows the proposal; the user clicks **Confirm** → `map_confirmed`, file written. If the proposal is off, load `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml` instead.
196	4. Full rule scan → `violation_found` (Scout: DR-1 in `news-summarize.ts`, red).
197	
198	## 11. The shell
199	
200	- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
201	- **Cell states:** looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned = amber · invariant hit = red · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step badges.
202	- **Agent cursor:** a small avatar pinned to the current cell, labeled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`", easing between cells in 250 ms.
203	- **Edges:** SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells; new edges draw in with a stroke-dashoffset animation.
204	- **Diff counts:** a +/− badge on each edited cell, ticking up.
205	- **Inspector:** click a cell or edge to see its paths, tables, invariants and provenance.
206	- **Replay:** a scrubber over the event index; dragging re-reduces the log.
207	- **Motion rule:** animate only state changes; nothing loops.
208	
209	## 12. Baseline run, for the pitch
210	
211	Copy `scout-agent` at the demo commit. In plain Claude Code, run "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K." Time it, then run `npm run proof`. If the new tool leaks personal data, time a follow-up turn that finds and fixes it. Those minutes are the "without" numbers the pitch converts the ledger into. If the baseline doesn't make the mistake, drop that comparison and lean on lines-to-review and memory.
212	
213	## 13. Build order and acceptance checks
214

49	    tools/       index.ts (the tool list)  web-search.ts  company-profile.ts  news-digest.ts  news-summarize.ts
50	    gateway/     complete.ts  embed.ts  redact.ts  cost-ledger.ts  providers.ts
51	    memory/      notes-store.ts  vector-index.ts  retrieve.ts
52	    outreach/    draft-email.ts  crm-sync.ts  send.ts  outreach-log.ts
53	  scripts/       dev.ts (runs API + web dev server)  proof.ts  seed.ts
54	  test/          channels/  orchestrator/  tools/  gateway/  memory/  outreach/
55	  web/           index.html  vite.config.ts  tsconfig.json
56	    src/main.tsx

58	    src/features/runs/       research form, run page, trail      (Agent loop)

64	```
65	
66	Feature folders never import each other; anything two features need lives in `web/src/shared/`.
67	
68	## Tables and their owners
69	
70	| Table | Written only from |
71	| --- | --- |
72	| `runs` | `src/orchestrator/` |
73	| `cost_log` | `src/gateway/` |
74	| `notes`, `embeddings` | `src/memory/` |
75	| `contacts`, `outreach_log` | `src/outreach/` |
76	
77	## How the parts fit
78	
79	- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/`): the only intended path to models. `complete({ purpose, messages })`, where `purpose` is one of `"plan" | "profile" | "summary" | "brief" | "email"`, redacts emails, phone numbers and known contact names into tokens like `[EMAIL_1]`, sends to the provider chosen in `providers.ts` (`vendor/llm-anthropic` by default, `vendor/llm-openai` when `SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai`) with an effort level per purpose, and appends a row to `cost_log` (tokens = characters / 4, fixed price table). Contact names come from `db.all("contacts")`; the gateway imports no other domain. `embed(text)` wraps `vendor/embeddings` the same way. No retries and no fallback between providers.
80	- **Redaction** (`src/gateway/redact.ts`): the phone pattern treats any run of seven or more digits separated by spaces, dots, dashes, commas or parentheses as a phone number. It catches every phone format in the fixtures, and it also turns full-precision figures such as `$4,512,300` into `$[PHONE_3]`. Every redaction applies to every purpose; there is no option to skip one. Nothing in the existing product checks figures: enrichment fixtures write money as `$4.5B`, and the gateway tests cover phone numbers, emails and names only.
81	- **Offline models** (`vendor/llm-*` with `SCOUT_MODE=offline`): canned answers from fixtures, keyed by a hash of the system prompt, for the prompts the product relies on (the planner's tool choice, email drafts). Any other prompt gets a deterministic extractive answer: the first three prose sentences of the last user message (lines of six or more words, with bullets and "Label:" prefixes stripped). Whatever the gateway sends is what comes back, tokens included, so the web app shows redaction tokens where a real model would have seen them.
82	- **Tools** (`src/tools/`): each tool is a `Tool` (`{ name, tags, description, run(input, ctx) }`, typed in `src/shared/types.ts`). `tools/index.ts` exports the list of all tools; tools never import the orchestrator. Tools only read. They use their vendors directly (search, news, sec-edgar, enrichment) and call models through the gateway. `news-digest` groups and formats headlines without a model call.
83	- **Orchestrator** (`src/orchestrator/`): `tool-registry.ts` imports the list from `../tools/index` and indexes it by name and tag. The run loop takes at most 6 steps. The planner calls `gateway.complete` with purpose `"plan"` to pick tools (the fake model's canned answer is fine), and also selects every registered tool whose `tags` match keywords in the goal. Run state goes to `runs`.
84	- **Memory** (`src/memory/`): stores notes per company, indexes them with `gateway.embed`, retrieves the top 3 for the brief.
85	- **Outreach** (`src/outreach/`): drafts an email via the gateway, upserts the contact in the fake CRM, writes `contacts` and `outreach_log`, and sends via the fake email vendor only when `send: true`.
86	- **Channels** (`src/channels/`): a JSON API under `/api` on `node:http` (runs, accounts and notes, contacts, outreach and sending a draft, usage, tools), which also serves the built web app, plus a CLI (`npm run scout -- --company Acme --contact jane@acme.com --goal "..."`). Validation lives in `validate.ts`.
87	
88	Every fake vendor returns deterministic output from `fixtures/` (keyed by a hash of the input, with a generic default) and appends to `vendor/_calllog.ts`.
89	
90	**Fixtures that later work depends on.** For each fixture company, `sec-edgar` has a 10-K and a 10-Q, each with an MD&A section and a financial table in full-precision figures. `news` has headlines that quote figures the same way, and one earnings call transcript (prepared remarks plus Q&A, with figures) that no tool uses yet.
91	
92	## Architecture rules the code follows
93	
94	The code follows all of these, **with exactly one exception**:
95	
96	1. Only `src/gateway/**` imports `vendor/llm-*` or `vendor/embeddings`. In `test/`, only `test/gateway/**` does.
97	2. Each table is written only by its owner (table above).
98	3. `src/tools/**` never imports `src/outreach/**`.
99	4. Dependencies point one way: channels → orchestrator → tools, memory, outreach → gateway. Nothing imports `src/channels/`; tools, memory and outreach never import the orchestrator; the gateway imports no other domain.
100	
101	**The one exception:** `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` imports `vendor/llm-anthropic/index` directly and calls it with the raw news text and contact context (in the system prompt), with no redaction and no cost logging. In live mode that sends the contact's details to the model provider for real. It must look like an ordinary, slightly hurried feature, not a bug: no comment, no TODO. Register it with tags `["news", "summary"]`. Its commit message gives the reason in one line of body, the way a hurried developer would: "Call the model client directly so revenue and deal figures in headlines come through intact."
102	
103	This matters for the demo. Later, an agent is asked to "add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K," and `news-summarize.ts` is the nearest example to copy. Its shortcut has a real reason: a 10-K summarized through the gateway comes back with its figures replaced by tokens. This holds on real filings: Symbotic's latest MD&A loses about 50 figures to `[PHONE_n]` tokens ("revenue $ [PHONE_22] $ [PHONE_23]"), Snowflake's about 86, because adjacent table figures and dates chain into seven-digit runs. So the agent faces a genuine choice between copying the shortcut and teaching the gateway about figures, which is real work in another domain, and both are reasonable to put to a person. A second request later asks for a tool that summarizes earnings call transcripts, which `vendor/news` already serves.
104	
105	## Proof script (`npm run proof`)
106	
107	- Runs the 20 requests in `fixtures/proof-requests.json` through the agent. Their contacts and goals contain personal data (emails, phone numbers, contact names), and goals mention news, filings and annual reports.
108	- Then, for each request, also invokes **every registered tool directly** once with that request's input, so any tool added later is exercised without editing the script.
109	- Reads the vendor call log and prints a large banner:
110	  - `PII reaching model providers: N of M model calls`
111	  - `Model calls missing from the cost log: K`
112	- With the exception above present, **N > 0**, all coming from `news-summarize`. A tool added later that routes through the gateway adds 0.
113	- Runs offline by default (deterministic numbers); `npm run proof -- --live` runs the same against live services.
114	- Exit code 0 regardless; this is a report, not a test.
115	
116	## Tests
117	
118	`vitest`, 2–4 tests per domain under `test/<domain>/`, about 20 in total, all passing in under 5 seconds. Each test file imports only from its own domain plus `shared` and `vendor`, so a test maps cleanly to one domain. Only `test/gateway/` may import `vendor/llm-*` or `vendor/embeddings`; tests in other domains that need a model call go through the gateway.
119	
120	## Git history
121	
122	Initialize a repo and commit in about 14 steps that read like real feature work, using conventional commit messages, in this order: scaffold → shared → vendor fakes and fixtures → gateway → memory → tools (search, profile, news digest) → orchestrator → channels → outreach → tests → proof script → web app → live providers (Claude, web search, SEC EDGAR; async runs) → finally `feat(tools): summarize recent news for the brief` (the exception, with the one-line body above) as the last commit.
123	
124	## README
125	
126	Product description, how to run (`npm i`, `npm run build` + `npm start`, `npm run dev`, `npm test`, `npm run proof`, the CLI), the API, a folder overview, and a short "Adding a tool" section that explains the tool list in `src/tools/index.ts` and tags and says "see `src/tools/` for examples." Do **not** describe the architecture rules.
127	
128	## Acceptance checks
129	
130	- [ ] `npm i && npm test` passes offline.
131	- [ ] `npm run proof` prints the banner with N > 0, and every leaking call comes from `news-summarize`.
132	- [ ] Imports of `vendor/llm-` or `vendor/embeddings` outside `src/gateway/` and `test/gateway/` appear in **exactly one file**: `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` (it imports `vendor/llm-anthropic`).
133	- [ ] With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, a run on a real company (e.g. Symbotic) completes live; `SCOUT_MODE=offline` runs everything without network.
134	- [ ] Every `db.insert(` / `db.update(` uses a double-quoted table literal that matches its owner directory.
135	- [ ] No file in `src/tools/` imports from `src/outreach/` or `src/orchestrator/`; no file in `src/gateway/` imports from another `src/` domain.
136	- [ ] Every relative import is extensionless; no `.js` specifiers anywhere.
137	- [ ] Passing a 10-K fixture through `complete()` returns text in which figures like `4,512,300` are replaced by `[PHONE_n]` tokens.
138	- [ ] `vendor/news` returns an earnings call transcript for each fixture company (offline) and finds one by web search (live).
139	- [ ] 2,500–3,500 lines in `src/`, `vendor/`, `scripts/`.
140	- [ ] None of the forbidden words appear in code, comments, commits or the README.
141	- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass; `npm start` serves the app and API on :8787.
142	- [ ] `web/src/features/*` folders don't import each other, and nothing in `web/` imports `src/` except `import type` from `src/shared/types`.
143	- [ ] `git log --oneline` shows about 14 feature commits, with the news summarizer last.

322	   111	export function normalizePath(path: string): string | null {

343	   132	export function resolvePath(path: string, exists: (path: string) => boolean): string | null {

346	   135	  const candidates = [base];

348	   137	  if (ext) for (const swap of EXT_SWAPS[ext]!) candidates.push(base.slice(0, -ext.length) + swap);

465	    93	/** Imports and writes that `newSource` adds over `oldSource` (multiset difference by target/table). */
466	    94	export function deltaForEdit(path: string, oldSource: string | null, newSource: string, exists: Exists): FactDelta {
467	    95	  const file = normalizePath(path) ?? path;
468	    96	  const before = oldSource === null ? null : counts(file, oldSource, exists);
469	    97	  const after = counts(file, newSource, exists);

483	   111	/** Cross-domain edges between cell files. Neutral, ignored, unassigned and test files, and same-domain imports, draw none. */
484	   112	export function domainEdges(facts: Facts | FactDelta, mapper: Mapper): DomainEdge[] {

486	   114	  for (const imp of facts.imports) {
487	   115	    const a = mapper.place(imp.from);
488	   116	    const b = mapper.place(imp.to);
489	   117	    if (a.kind !== 'cell' || b.kind !== 'cell' || a.domain === b.domain) continue;
490	   118	    const key = `${a.domain}\u0000${b.domain}`;
491	   119	    let edge = edges.get(key);
492	   120	    if (!edge) edges.set(key, (edge = { from: a.domain, to: b.domain, files: [] }));
493	   121	    edge.files.push(imp);
494	   122	  }
495	   123	  return [...edges.values()].sort((x, y) => x.from.localeCompare(y.from) || x.to.localeCompare(y.to));

673	     6	/** End of the source line on which `node`'s value ends (before any trailing comment's newline). */
674	     7	function lineEndAfter(text: string, node: Node): number {
675	     8	  let p = node.range![1];
676	     9	  while (p > 0 && /\s/.test(text[p - 1]!)) p--;
677	    10	  const nl = text.indexOf('\n', p);
678	    11	  return nl === -1 ? text.length : nl;
679	    12	}
680	    13	
681	    14	function column(text: string, offset: number): number {
682	    15	  return offset - (text.lastIndexOf('\n', offset - 1) + 1);
683	    16	}
684	    17	
685	    18	/**
686	    19	 * Append `value` to the list at `key` of invariant `invariantId`, creating the key if missing.
687	    20	 * Splices text into the original so comments, spacing and alignment elsewhere are untouched.
688	    21	 */
689	    22	function appendToInvariant(yamlText: string, invariantId: string, key: string, value: unknown): string {
690	    23	  const doc = YAML.parseDocument(yamlText);
691	    24	  const list = doc.get('invariants');
692	    25	  const inv = isSeq(list) ? list.items.find((item) => isMap(item) && item.get('id') === invariantId) : undefined;
693	    26	  if (!isMap(inv) || inv.items.length === 0) throw new Error(`domains.yaml has no invariant ${invariantId}`);
694	    27	  const splice = (at: number, insert: string) => yamlText.slice(0, at) + insert + yamlText.slice(at);
695	    28	  const item = flow(value);
696	    29	  const seq = inv.get(key, true);
697	    30	
698	    31	  if (isSeq(seq) && seq.flow) {
699	    32	    const close = yamlText.lastIndexOf(']', seq.range![1] - 1);
700	    33	    return splice(close, seq.items.length ? `, ${item}` : item);
701	    34	  }
702	    35	  if (isSeq(seq)) {
703	    36	    const last = seq.items.at(-1) as Node | undefined;
704	    37	    if (!last) throw new Error(`${invariantId}.${key} is malformed`);
705	    38	    return splice(lineEndAfter(yamlText, last), `\n${' '.repeat(column(yamlText, seq.range![0]))}- ${item}`);
706	    39	  }
707	    40	  if (seq !== undefined && seq !== null) throw new Error(`${invariantId}.${key} is not a list`);
708	    41	  const firstKey = inv.items[0]!.key as Node;
709	    42	  const lastPair = inv.items.at(-1)!;
710	    43	  const end = lineEndAfter(yamlText, (lastPair.value ?? lastPair.key) as Node);
711	    44	  return splice(end, `\n${' '.repeat(column(yamlText, firstKey.range![0]))}${key}: [${item}]`);
712	    45	}

    43	    edges: { from: string; to: string; steps: number[]; imports: ImportEdge[] }[];
    44	    unassigned: string[];
    45	  };
    46	  plan_violation: { violation: Violation };
    47	  fork_asked: { violations: Violation[]; text: string };
    48	  fork_answered: { option: 'A' | 'B'; text: string; violations: Violation[] };
    49	  plan_approved: Record<string, never>;

    51	  edited: { added: number; removed: number; created: boolean; unattributed?: boolean; tool?: string };
    52	  edge_added: { edge: ImportEdge; from: string; to: string };
    53	  edge_removed: { edge: ImportEdge; from: string; to: string };

    62	export const cellKey = (c: Cell) => `${c.domain}/${c.layer}`;
    63	export const edgeKey = (from: string, to: string) => `${from}->${to}`;

    68	export type TurnState = {

    78	  violationsSeen: { v: Violation; source: 'plan' | 'gate' }[]; // every violation raised in the turn, for the ledger
    79	  looked: Record<string, string[]>; // cellKey → paths
    80	  edited: Record<string, { added: number; removed: number; files: string[]; created: string[]; unattributed: boolean }>;

    84	  edgesRemoved: { from: string; to: string; edge: ImportEdge }[];
    85	  forks: { asked: number; answered: number | null; option: 'A' | 'B' | null; violations: Violation[]; beforeCode: boolean }[];

    96	export type UIState = {
    97	  map: DomainMap | null;
    98	  files: Record<string, Placement>;
    99	  edges: Record<string, DomainEdgeState>;

   101	  turns: TurnState[];
   102	  current: string | null;
   103	  cursor: { cell: Cell | null; path: string; verb: string } | null;
   104	  chat: { role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'; text: string; turn: string | null; t: number }[];
   105	  awaitingApproval: { turn: string | null; plan: string } | null;
   106	  pendingFork: { turn: string | null; violations: Violation[] } | null;
   107	  decisions: Decision[];

   114	export function initialState(): UIState {
   115	  return {
   116	    map: null, files: {}, edges: {}, violations: [], turns: [], current: null, cursor: null, chat: [],
   117	    awaitingApproval: null, pendingFork: null, decisions: [], errors: [], edgeOrigin: {}, cellOrigin: {},
   118	  };
   119	}

   121	function newTurn(id: string, prompt: string, t: number): TurnState {
   122	  return {
   123	    id, prompt, startedAt: t, endedAt: null, steps: [], planned: {}, plannedEdges: {}, planViolations: [], gateBlocks: [], violationsSeen: [],
   124	    looked: {}, edited: {}, tests: {}, unassigned: [], edgesAdded: [], edgesRemoved: [], forks: [], decisions: [],
   125	    approved: false, firstEditAt: null, numstat: null,
   126	  };
   127	}

   129	const push = <T>(rec: Record<string, T[]>, k: string, v: T) => { (rec[k] ??= []).push(v); };

   131	/** Fold one event into the state. Mutates and returns `s`; callers that need immutability use `reduce`. */
   132	export function apply(s: UIState, e: HarnessEvent, index: number): UIState {
   133	  const turn = e.turn ? s.turns.find((x) => x.id === e.turn) ?? null : null;
   134	  const d = (e.data ?? {}) as never;
   135	
   136	  switch (e.kind) {
   137	    case 'map_confirmed':
   138	    case 'map_proposed': {
   139	      const { map } = d as EventData['map_confirmed'];
   140	      s.map = map;
   141	      break;
   142	    }
   143	    case 'repo_scanned': {
   144	      const { files, edges } = d as EventData['repo_scanned'];
   145	      s.files = {};
   146	      for (const f of files) s.files[f.path] = f.placement;
   147	      s.edges = {};
   148	      for (const ed of edges) s.edges[edgeKey(ed.from, ed.to)] = { from: ed.from, to: ed.to, files: [...ed.files] };
   149	      break;
   150	    }
   151	    case 'file_assigned': {
   152	      if (e.path) s.files[e.path] = (d as EventData['file_assigned']).placement;
   153	      break;
   154	    }
   155	    case 'violation_found':
   156	      s.violations = (d as EventData['violation_found']).violations;
   157	      break;
   158	    case 'turn_started': {
   159	      const t = newTurn(e.turn ?? e.id, (d as EventData['turn_started']).prompt, e.t);
   160	      s.turns.push(t);
   161	      s.current = t.id;
   162	      s.cursor = null;
   163	      break;
   164	    }
   165	    case 'chat': {
   166	      const { role, text } = d as EventData['chat'];
   167	      s.chat.push({ role, text, turn: e.turn, t: e.t });
   168	      break;
   169	    }
   170	    case 'looked':
   171	    case 'cursor': {
   172	      if (e.path) s.cursor = { cell: e.cell ?? null, path: e.path, verb: e.kind === 'cursor' ? (d as EventData['cursor']).verb : 'reading' };
   173	      if (e.kind === 'looked' && turn && e.cell && e.path) {
   174	        const k = cellKey(e.cell);
   175	        const list = (turn.looked[k] ??= []);
   176	        if (!list.includes(e.path)) list.push(e.path);
   177	      }
   178	      break;
   179	    }
   180	    case 'planned': {
   181	      if (!turn) break;
   182	      const p = d as EventData['planned'];
   183	      turn.steps = p.steps;
   184	      turn.planned = {};
   185	      for (const c of p.cells) turn.planned[cellKey(c)] = { cell: { domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer }, steps: c.steps, files: c.files };
   186	      turn.plannedEdges = {};
   187	      for (const ed of p.edges) turn.plannedEdges[edgeKey(ed.from, ed.to)] = ed;
   188	      turn.unassigned = p.unassigned;
   189	      turn.planViolations = []; // a resubmitted plan replaces the previous one's violations
   190	      break;
   191	    }
   192	    case 'plan_violation': {
   193	      const { violation } = d as EventData['plan_violation'];
   194	      turn?.planViolations.push(violation);
   195	      turn?.violationsSeen.push({ v: violation, source: 'plan' });
   196	      break;
   197	    }
   198	    case 'gate_blocked': {
   199	      const { violation } = d as EventData['gate_blocked'];
   200	      turn?.gateBlocks.push(violation);
   201	      turn?.violationsSeen.push({ v: violation, source: 'gate' });
   202	      break;
   203	    }
   204	    case 'fork_asked': {
   205	      const { violations } = d as EventData['fork_asked'];
   206	      s.pendingFork = { turn: e.turn, violations };
   207	      turn?.forks.push({ asked: index, answered: null, option: null, violations, beforeCode: turn.firstEditAt === null });
   208	      break;
   209	    }
   210	    case 'fork_answered': {
   211	      const { option } = d as EventData['fork_answered'];
   212	      s.pendingFork = null;
   213	      const f = turn?.forks.findLast((x) => x.answered === null);
   214	      if (f) { f.answered = index; f.option = option; f.beforeCode = f.beforeCode && turn!.firstEditAt === null; }
   215	      if (turn) turn.gateBlocks = []; // answered; the decision now governs
   216	      break;
   217	    }
   218	    case 'approval_requested':
   219	      s.awaitingApproval = { turn: e.turn, plan: (d as EventData['approval_requested']).plan };
   220	      break;
   221	    case 'plan_approved':
   222	      s.awaitingApproval = null;
   223	      if (turn) turn.approved = true;
   224	      break;
   225	    case 'edited': {
   226	      const ed = d as EventData['edited'];
   227	      if (s.cursor && e.path && !ed.unattributed) s.cursor = { cell: e.cell ?? null, path: e.path, verb: 'editing' };
   228	      if (!turn || !e.path) break;
   229	      if (turn.firstEditAt === null) turn.firstEditAt = index;
   230	      const placement = s.files[e.path];
   231	      if (placement?.kind === 'test') { push(turn.tests, placement.domain, e.path); break; }
   232	      if (!e.cell) { if (!turn.unassigned.includes(e.path)) turn.unassigned.push(e.path); break; }
   233	      const k = cellKey(e.cell);
   234	      const c = (turn.edited[k] ??= { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], created: [], unattributed: false });
   235	      c.added += ed.added;
   236	      c.removed += ed.removed;
   237	      if (!c.files.includes(e.path)) c.files.push(e.path);
   238	      if (ed.created && !c.created.includes(e.path)) c.created.push(e.path);
   239	      if (ed.unattributed) c.unattributed = true;
   240	      push(s.cellOrigin, k, { turn: e.turn, at: index });
   241	      break;
   242	    }
   243	    case 'edge_added': {
   244	      const { edge, from, to } = d as EventData['edge_added'];
   245	      const k = edgeKey(from, to);
   246	      const cur = (s.edges[k] ??= { from, to, files: [] });
   247	      if (!cur.files.some((f) => f.from === edge.from && f.to === edge.to)) cur.files.push(edge);
   248	      push(s.edgeOrigin, k, { turn: e.turn, at: index });
   249	      turn?.edgesAdded.push({ from, to, edge });
   250	      break;
   251	    }
   252	    case 'edge_removed': {
   253	      const { edge, from, to } = d as EventData['edge_removed'];
   254	      const k = edgeKey(from, to);
   255	      const cur = s.edges[k];
   256	      if (cur) {
   257	        cur.files = cur.files.filter((f) => !(f.from === edge.from && f.to === edge.to));
   258	        if (!cur.files.length) delete s.edges[k];
   259	      }
   260	      turn?.edgesRemoved.push({ from, to, edge });
   261	      break;
   262	    }
   263	    case 'decision_recorded': {
   264	      const dec = d as EventData['decision_recorded'];
   265	      const existing = s.decisions.find((x) => x.id === dec.id);
   266	      if (existing) Object.assign(existing, dec); // the Alike confirmation re-emits with alike: true
   267	      else s.decisions.push({ ...dec, turn: e.turn, at: index });
   268	      if (turn && !turn.decisions.includes(dec.id)) turn.decisions.push(dec.id);
   269	      break;
   270	    }
   271	    case 'turn_ended': {
   272	      if (!turn) break;
   273	      const { added, removed } = d as EventData['turn_ended'];
   274	      turn.endedAt = e.t;
   275	      turn.numstat = { added, removed };
   276	      s.awaitingApproval = null;
   277	      if (s.current === turn.id) s.cursor = null;
   278	      break;
   279	    }
   280	    case 'error':
   281	      s.errors.push((d as EventData['error']).message);
   282	      break;
   283	    case 'test_result':
   284	      break;
   285	  }
   286	  return s;
   287	}
   288	
   289	/** UI state = reduce(events). Replay is `reduce(events, i)`: the state after the first `i` events. */
   290	export function reduce(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo = events.length): UIState {
   291	  const s = initialState();
   292	  const n = Math.min(upTo, events.length);
   293	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) apply(s, events[i]!, i);
   294	  return s;
   295	}

   297	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- derived views
   298	
   299	export type CellView = {
   300	  cell: Cell;
   301	  looked: boolean;
   302	  edited: boolean;
   303	  ghost: number[] | null; // planned step numbers while not yet edited
   304	  unplanned: boolean; // amber: edited but not in this turn's plan
   305	  violation: 'existing' | 'new' | null;
   306	  violationFiles: string[];
   307	  newViolationFiles: string[];
   308	  added: number;
   309	  removed: number;
   310	};
   311	
   312	/** Per-cell visual state for one turn (defaults to the latest), plus load-time violations. */
   313	export function cellViews(s: UIState, turnId: string | null = s.turns.at(-1)?.id ?? null): Record<string, CellView> {
   314	  const out: Record<string, CellView> = {};
   315	  const map = s.map;
   316	  if (!map) return out;
   317	  const turn = turnId ? s.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId) ?? null : null;
   318	  const hasPlan = !!turn && Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;
   319	
   320	  for (const dom of map.domains) {
   321	    for (const layer of map.layers) {
   322	      if (!(layer.id in dom.cells)) continue;
   323	      const cell = { domain: dom.id, layer: layer.id };
   324	      const k = cellKey(cell);
   325	      const edited = turn?.edited[k];
   326	      const planned = turn?.planned[k];
   327	      out[k] = {
   328	        cell,
   329	        looked: !!turn?.looked[k]?.length,
   330	        edited: !!edited,
   331	        ghost: planned && !edited ? planned.steps : null,
   332	        unplanned: hasPlan && !!edited && !planned,
   333	        violation: null,
   334	        violationFiles: [],
   335	        newViolationFiles: [],
   336	        added: edited?.added ?? 0,
   337	        removed: edited?.removed ?? 0,
   338	      };
   339	    }
   340	  }
   341	  const mark = (file: string, isNew: boolean, planCell?: Cell) => {
   342	    const p = s.files[file];
   343	    const cell = p?.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : planCell;
   344	    if (!cell) return;
   345	    const v = out[cellKey(cell)];
   346	    if (!v) return;
   347	    if (isNew) {
   348	      v.violation = 'new';
   349	      if (!v.newViolationFiles.includes(file)) v.newViolationFiles.push(file);
   350	    } else {
   351	      v.violation ??= 'existing';
   352	      if (!v.violationFiles.includes(file)) v.violationFiles.push(file);
   353	    }
   354	  };
   355	  for (const v of s.violations) mark(v.file, false);
   356	  if (turn) {
   357	    const plannedCellOf = (file: string) => Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file))?.cell;
   358	    for (const v of [...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks]) {
   359	      if (s.violations.some((x) => x.file === v.file && x.invariant === v.invariant)) continue; // already on the map before this turn
   360	      mark(v.file, true, plannedCellOf(v.file));
   361	    }
   362	  }
   363	  return out;
   364	}
   365	
   366	export type EdgeView = {
   367	  from: string;
   368	  to: string;
   369	  state: 'existing' | 'ghost' | 'new';
   370	  violation: boolean;
   371	  steps: number[];
   372	  files: ImportEdge[];
   373	};
   374	
   375	/**
   376	 * Edges for one turn. A planned edge always gets its own `ghost` entry, even when a solid edge between the same
   377	 * domains exists, so a plan that repeats an existing violation still looks different from the map before the turn.
   378	 */
   379	export function edgeViews(s: UIState, turnId: string | null = s.turns.at(-1)?.id ?? null): EdgeView[] {
   380	  const turn = turnId ? s.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId) ?? null : null;
   381	  const violating = (from: string, files: ImportEdge[], list: Violation[]) =>
   382	    list.some((v) => files.some((f) => f.from === v.file && (!v.target || v.target === f.to)));
   383	  const out: EdgeView[] = [];
   384	  const addedThisTurn = new Set(turn?.edgesAdded.map((x) => edgeKey(x.from, x.to)) ?? []);
   385	  for (const [k, e] of Object.entries(s.edges)) {
   386	    out.push({ from: e.from, to: e.to, state: addedThisTurn.has(k) ? 'new' : 'existing', violation: violating(e.from, e.files, s.violations), steps: [], files: e.files });
   387	  }
   388	  if (turn) {
   389	    for (const pe of Object.values(turn.plannedEdges)) {
   390	      const built = pe.imports.every((imp) => s.edges[edgeKey(pe.from, pe.to)]?.files.some((f) => f.from === imp.from && f.to === imp.to));
   391	      if (built) continue;
   392	      out.push({ from: pe.from, to: pe.to, state: 'ghost', violation: violating(pe.from, pe.imports, turn.planViolations), steps: pe.steps, files: pe.imports });
   393	    }
   394	  }
   395	  return out;
   396	}
   397	
   398	/** Decisions and turns behind an edge or a cell, for the inspector. */
   399	export function provenance(s: UIState, target: { edge: string } | { cell: string }) {
   400	  const origins = 'edge' in target ? s.edgeOrigin[target.edge] ?? [] : s.cellOrigin[target.cell] ?? [];
   401	  const turnIds = [...new Set(origins.map((o) => o.turn).filter((x): x is string => !!x))];
   402	  const turns = turnIds.map((id) => ({ id, index: s.turns.findIndex((t) => t.id === id) + 1, prompt: s.turns.find((t) => t.id === id)?.prompt ?? '' }));
   403	  const decisions = s.decisions.filter((d) => d.turn && turnIds.includes(d.turn));
   404	  return { turns, decisions };
   405	}
     1	import { cellKey, type Cell, type TurnState, type UIState } from './events';
     2	import type { Violation } from './rules';
     3	
     4	export type Severity = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;
     5	
     6	export type Finding = {
     7	  severity: Severity;
     8	  kind: 'invariant' | 'new_edge' | 'new_external' | 'unplanned' | 'planned';
     9	  cell: Cell | null;
    10	  text: string;
    11	  files: string[];
    12	  invariant?: string;
    13	};
    14	
    15	export type TurnLedger = {
    16	  turn: string;
    17	  linesChanged: number | null; // null until turn_ended brings the git numstat
    18	  cellsToReview: number;
    19	  forksCaughtBeforeCode: number;
    20	  rejectedOptionsBlocked: number;
    21	  findings: Finding[];
    22	};
    23	
    24	export type Ledger = {
    25	  turns: TurnLedger[];
    26	  session: { linesChanged: number; cellsToReview: number; forksCaughtBeforeCode: number; rejectedOptionsBlocked: number };
    27	};
    28	
    29	const vkey = (v: Violation) => `${v.invariant}|${v.file}|${v.target ?? ''}`;
    30	
    31	function cellOf(s: UIState, turn: TurnState, file: string): Cell | null {
    32	  const p = s.files[file];
    33	  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer };
    34	  const edited = Object.entries(turn.edited).find(([, c]) => c.files.includes(file));
    35	  if (edited) { const [domain, layer] = edited[0].split('/') as [string, string]; return { domain, layer }; }
    36	  return Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file))?.cell ?? null;
    37	}
    38	
    39	/** Severity-ranked findings for one turn (SPEC §9): 1 invariant hit · 2 new edge / new external · 3 unplanned · 4 planned. */
    40	export function turnFindings(s: UIState, turn: TurnState): Finding[] {
    41	  const out: Finding[] = [];
    42	  const seen = new Set<string>();
    43	  for (const { v } of turn.violationsSeen) {
    44	    if (seen.has(vkey(v))) continue;
    45	    seen.add(vkey(v));
    46	    out.push({ severity: 1, kind: 'invariant', cell: cellOf(s, turn, v.file), text: v.reason, files: [v.file], invariant: v.invariant });
    47	  }
    48	  const edges = new Map<string, { from: string; to: string; files: string[] }>();
    49	  for (const e of turn.edgesAdded) {
    50	    const k = `${e.from}->${e.to}`;
    51	    const cur = edges.get(k) ?? { from: e.from, to: e.to, files: [] };
    52	    if (!cur.files.includes(e.edge.from)) cur.files.push(e.edge.from);
    53	    edges.set(k, cur);
    54	  }
    55	  for (const e of edges.values()) {
    56	    const cell = cellOf(s, turn, e.files[0]!);
    57	    out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_edge', cell, text: `New dependency: ${name(s, e.from)} → ${name(s, e.to)}`, files: e.files });
    58	  }
    59	  const hasPlan = Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;
    60	  for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(turn.edited)) {
    61	    const [domain, layer] = k.split('/') as [string, string];
    62	    const cell = { domain, layer };
    63	    if (layer === 'external' && c.created.length) {
    64	      out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_external', cell, text: `New external service in ${name(s, domain)}`, files: c.created });
    65	    }
    66	    if (hasPlan && !turn.planned[k]) {
    67	      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell, text: `Edited ${name(s, domain)} · ${layer} without planning it`, files: c.files });
    68	    } else {
    69	      out.push({ severity: 4, kind: 'planned', cell, text: `${name(s, domain)} · ${layer}: ${c.files.length} file(s), +${c.added} −${c.removed}`, files: c.files });
    70	    }
    71	  }
    72	  for (const file of turn.unassigned) {
    73	    if (hasPlan && !Object.values(turn.planned).some((c) => c.files.includes(file))) {
    74	      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell: null, text: `Edited ${file}, which belongs to no domain`, files: [file] });
    75	    }
    76	  }
    77	  return out.sort((a, b) => a.severity - b.severity);
    78	}
    79	
    80	function name(s: UIState, domain: string) {
    81	  return s.map?.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.name ?? domain;
    82	}

    85	  const findings = turnFindings(s, turn);
    86	  const review = new Set(findings.filter((f) => f.severity <= 3).map((f) => (f.cell ? cellKey(f.cell) : `file:${f.files[0]}`)));

    88	  let forks = 0;

    96	    linesChanged: turn.numstat ? turn.numstat.added + turn.numstat.removed : null,
    97	    cellsToReview: review.size,
    98	    forksCaughtBeforeCode: forks,
    99	    rejectedOptionsBlocked: rejected,
   100	    findings,
   101	  };
   102	}

   104	export function ledger(s: UIState): Ledger {
   105	  const turns = s.turns.map((t) => turnLedger(s, t));

   109	    session: {

   111	      cellsToReview: sum((t) => t.cellsToReview),

439	    53	export function bashWriteTarget(cmd: string, rel: (p: string) => string | null): string | null {
440	    54	  const inRepo = (p: string) => !!p && !p.startsWith('/dev/') && rel(p.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '')) !== null;

442	    56	  for (const m of cmd.matchAll(/(?:^|[^0-9&>])>>?\s*([^\s;&|<>()]+)/g)) if (!m[1]!.startsWith('&') && inRepo(m[1]!)) return `redirect to ${m[1]}`;
443	    57	  for (const m of cmd.matchAll(/\btee\s+(?:-a\s+)?([^\s;&|<>()]+)/g)) if (inRepo(m[1]!)) return `tee ${m[1]}`;
444	    58	  if (/\b(sed|perl)\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*\s+)*-[a-zA-Z]*i/.test(cmd)) return 'in-place edit';

1021	    16	/** Turn baseline: HEAD plus a `git stash create` snapshot of the working tree (no stash entry is stored). */
1022	    17	export function baseline(repo: string): Baseline {
1023	    18	  const head = tryGit(repo, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD']);
1024	    19	  const snapshot = tryGit(repo, ['stash', 'create']) || head;

1028	    23	
1029	    24	function untrackedFiles(repo: string): string[] {

1031	    26	}
1032	    27	
1033	    28	/** Lines added/removed since the baseline, including files created during the turn (untracked). */
1034	    29	export function numstat(repo: string, base: Baseline): { added: number; removed: number; files: string[] } {
1035	    30	  let added = 0, removed = 0;
1036	    31	  const files: string[] = [];
1037	    32	  const parse = (out: string, name?: string) => {
1038	    33	    for (const line of out.split('\n')) {
1039	    34	      const [a, r, ...rest] = line.split('\t');
1040	    35	      if (!rest.length) continue;
1041	    36	      added += Number(a) || 0;
1042	    37	      removed += Number(r) || 0;
1043	    38	      files.push(name ?? rest.join('\t'));
1044	    39	    }
1045	    40	  };
1046	    41	  if (base.snapshot) parse(tryGit(repo, ['diff', '--numstat', base.snapshot, '--', '.', ...HARNESS_PATHS]));

1048	    43	  for (const f of untrackedFiles(repo)) {
1049	    44	    if (before.has(f) || f.startsWith('decisions/') || f.startsWith('.harness/') || f === 'domains.yaml') continue;

166	type ServerMsg =

172	const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
173	/** Dev-only: `?fake=1` loads /fake-events.json at once, `?fake=play` streams it; `&at=N` opens the replay at N. */
174	export const fakeMode = params.get('fake');
175	
176	export function connect() {
177	  if (fakeMode) return loadFake(fakeMode === 'play');
178	  void fetch('/api/info')
179	    .then((r) => r.json() as Promise<{ repo: string }>)
180	    .then((i) => useStore.getState().setRepo(i.repo))
181	    .catch(() => {});
182	  openSocket(500);
183	}
184	
185	function openSocket(delay: number) {
186	  const ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws`);
187	  let opened = false;
188	  ws.onopen = () => {
189	    opened = true;
190	    useStore.getState().setConn('open');
191	  };
192	  ws.onmessage = (m) => {
193	    const msg = JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerMsg;
194	    const s = useStore.getState();
195	    if (msg.type === 'hello') s.hello(msg.events, msg.busy);
196	    else if (msg.type === 'event') s.append(msg.event);
197	    else if (msg.type === 'delta') s.addDelta(msg.text);
198	    else if (msg.type === 'busy') s.setBusy(msg.busy);
199	  };
200	  ws.onclose = () => {
201	    useStore.getState().setConn('down');
202	    const next = opened ? 500 : Math.min(delay * 2, 8000);
203	    setTimeout(() => openSocket(next), opened ? 500 : delay);
204	  };
205	}
206	
207	async function loadFake(play: boolean) {
208	  const st = useStore.getState();
209	  st.setConn('fake');
210	  st.setRepo('scout-agent (fake turn)');
211	  const events = (await (await fetch('/fake-events.json')).json()) as HarnessEvent[];
212	  const at = params.get('at');
213	  if (!play) {
214	    st.hello(events, false);
215	    if (at !== null) st.setReplay(Math.max(0, Math.min(events.length, Number(at))));
216	    return;
217	  }
218	  st.hello([], false);
219	  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
220	    const e = events[i]!;
221	    const prev = events[i - 1];
222	    const gap = prev ? Math.max(20, Math.min(900, (e.t - prev.t) / 3)) : 0;
223	    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, e.kind === 'file_assigned' ? 15 : gap));
224	    useStore.getState().append(e);
225	  }
226	}

271	let reduceCache: { events: readonly HarnessEvent[]; upTo: number; ui: UIState } | null = null;
272	let viewCache: { ui: UIState; turnSel: string | null; view: View } | null = null;
273	
274	function reduced(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo: number): UIState {
275	  if (reduceCache && reduceCache.events === events && reduceCache.upTo === upTo) return reduceCache.ui;
276	  const ui = reduce(events, upTo);
277	  reduceCache = { events, upTo, ui };
278	  return ui;
279	}

281	export function deriveView(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], replay: number | null, turnSel: string | null): View {
282	  const upTo = replay ?? events.length;
283	  const ui = reduced(events, upTo);
284	  if (viewCache && viewCache.ui === ui && viewCache.turnSel === turnSel) return viewCache.view;
285	
286	  const turn = (turnSel && ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnSel)) || ui.turns.at(-1) || null;
287	  const cellFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
288	  const testFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
289	  const unassigned: string[] = [];
290	  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) {
291	    if (p.kind === 'cell') (cellFiles[cellKey(p)] ??= []).push(path);
292	    else if (p.kind === 'test') (testFiles[p.domain] ??= []).push(path);
293	    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned.push(path);
294	  }
295	  for (const list of Object.values(cellFiles)) list.sort();
296	
297	  let proposed = -1;
298	  let confirmed = -1;
299	  const turnStarts: number[] = [];
300	  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
301	    const k = events[i]!.kind;
302	    if (k === 'turn_started') turnStarts.push(i);
303	    if (i >= upTo) continue;
304	    if (k === 'map_proposed') proposed = i;
305	    if (k === 'map_confirmed') confirmed = i;
306	  }
307	  const proposal = proposed > confirmed && ui.map ? { domains: ui.map.domains.length, rules: ui.map.invariants.length } : null;
308	
309	  const l = ledger(ui);
310	  const view: View = {
311	    ui,
312	    upTo,
313	    live: replay === null,
314	    turn,
315	    turnIndex: turn ? ui.turns.indexOf(turn) + 1 : 0,
316	    cells: cellViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
317	    edges: edgeViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
318	    ledger: l,
319	    turnLedger: turn ? turnLedger(ui, turn) : null,
320	    cellFiles,
321	    testFiles,
322	    unassigned,
323	    proposal,
324	    steps: turn ? stepProgress(turn) : { done: 0, total: 0 },
325	    turnStarts,
326	  };
327	  viewCache = { ui, turnSel, view };
328	  return view;
329	}

331	/** "3 of 6 steps": a step is done when every cell it plans has been edited (or, for a step with no cells, its files). */
332	function stepProgress(turn: TurnState) {
333	  const editedFiles = new Set([
334	    ...Object.values(turn.edited).flatMap((c) => c.files),
335	    ...Object.values(turn.tests).flat(),
336	    ...turn.unassigned,
337	  ]);
338	  let done = 0;
339	  for (const step of turn.steps) {
340	    const cells = Object.entries(turn.planned).filter(([, c]) => c.steps.includes(step.n)).map(([k]) => k);
341	    const ok = cells.length ? cells.every((k) => !!turn.edited[k]) : step.files.length > 0 && step.files.every((f) => editedFiles.has(f));
342	    if (ok) done++;
343	  }
344	  return { done, total: turn.steps.length };
345	}

350	  const turnSel = useStore((s) => s.turn);
351	  return deriveView(events, replay, turnSel);

355	export function turnViolations(v: View): { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] {
356	  const out: { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] = v.ui.violations.map((x) => ({ v: x, source: 'load' as const }));
357	  for (const x of v.turn?.planViolations ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'plan' });

371	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
372	
373	export const reducedMotion = () => typeof matchMedia !== 'undefined' && matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
374	
375	/** Counts up (or down) to `value` over ~400 ms whenever it changes. */
376	export function useTween(value: number, ms = 400): number {
377	  const [shown, setShown] = useState(value);
378	  const from = useRef(value);
379	  useEffect(() => {
380	    if (reducedMotion() || from.current === value) {
381	      from.current = value;
382	      setShown(value);
383	      return;
384	    }
385	    const start = performance.now();
386	    const a = from.current;
387	    let raf = 0;
388	    const step = (now: number) => {
389	      const k = Math.min(1, (now - start) / ms);
390	      const eased = 1 - (1 - k) ** 3;
391	      setShown(Math.round(a + (value - a) * eased));
392	      if (k < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
393	      else from.current = value;
394	    };
395	    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
396	    return () => {
397	      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
398	      from.current = value;
399	    };
400	  }, [value, ms]);
401	  return shown;
402	}
403	
404	/** True for a moment after `key` changes (not on mount). */
405	export function useFlash(key: unknown, ms = 650): boolean {
406	  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
407	  const first = useRef(true);
408	  useEffect(() => {
409	    if (first.current) {
410	      first.current = false;
411	      return;
412	    }
413	    setOn(true);
414	    const t = setTimeout(() => setOn(false), ms);
415	    return () => clearTimeout(t);
416	  }, [key, ms]);
417	  return on;
418	}

420	export function useSize<T extends HTMLElement>() {
421	  const ref = useRef<T>(null);
422	  const [size, setSize] = useState({ w: 0, h: 0 });
423	  useEffect(() => {
424	    const el = ref.current;
425	    if (!el) return;
426	    const ro = new ResizeObserver(([e]) => {
427	      if (e) setSize({ w: e.contentRect.width, h: e.contentRect.height });
428	    });
429	    ro.observe(el);
430	    return () => ro.disconnect();
431	  }, []);
432	  return [ref, size] as const;
433	}

435	import { cellKey, type DomainMap, type EdgeView, type ImportEdge, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation } from '@harness/core/view';
436	
437	export type Rect = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };
438	
439	export type GridLayout = {
440	  width: number;
441	  height: number;
442	  labelW: number;
443	  headerH: number;
444	  gapX: number;
445	  gapY: number;
446	  colW: number;
447	  rowH: number;
448	  cols: { id: string; name: string; purpose: string; x: number; index: number }[];
449	  rows: { id: string; name: string; y: number; index: number }[];
450	  cells: Record<string, Rect & { col: number; row: number }>;
451	  unassigned: Rect | null;
452	};
453	
454	/** Fixed grid: a gutter on both sides of every column and row, so edges can route around cells. */
455	export function gridLayout(map: DomainMap, size: { w: number; h: number }, withUnassigned: boolean): GridLayout {
456	  const labelW = 64;
457	  const headerH = 46;
458	  const n = map.domains.length + (withUnassigned ? 1 : 0);
459	  const r = map.layers.length;
460	  const gapX = Math.max(28, Math.min(44, size.w * 0.032));
461	  const gapY = 26;
462	  const colW = Math.max(96, (size.w - labelW - gapX * (n + 1)) / n);
463	  const rowH = Math.max(72, Math.min(150, (size.h - headerH - gapY * (r + 1)) / r));
464	  const colX = (i: number) => labelW + gapX + i * (colW + gapX);
465	  const rowY = (j: number) => headerH + gapY + j * (rowH + gapY);
466	  const cols = map.domains.map((d, i) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose, x: colX(i), index: i }));
467	  const rows = map.layers.map((l, j) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name, y: rowY(j), index: j }));
468	  const cells: GridLayout['cells'] = {};
469	  map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
470	    map.layers.forEach((l, j) => {
471	      if (l.id in d.cells) cells[cellKey({ domain: d.id, layer: l.id })] = { x: colX(i), y: rowY(j), w: colW, h: rowH, col: i, row: j };
472	    });
473	  });
474	  const unassigned = withUnassigned ? { x: colX(n - 1), y: rowY(0), w: colW, h: rowY(r - 1) + rowH - rowY(0) } : null;
475	  if (withUnassigned) cols.push({ id: '__unassigned', name: 'Unassigned', purpose: 'Files that match no cell in domains.yaml', x: colX(n - 1), index: n - 1 });
476	  return {
477	    width: labelW + gapX * (n + 1) + colW * n,
478	    height: headerH + gapY * (r + 1) + rowH * r,
479	    labelW, headerH, gapX, gapY, colW, rowH, cols, rows, cells, unassigned,
480	  };
481	}

485	export type EdgeSegment = {
486	  key: string; // stable React key
487	  edgeKey: string; // `${from}->${to}`
488	  pair: string; // `${srcCell}=>${dstCell}`
489	  from: string;
490	  to: string;
491	  src: string; // cellKey
492	  dst: string; // cellKey
493	  state: EdgeView['state'];
494	  violation: boolean;
495	  steps: number[];
496	  files: ImportEdge[];
497	};
498	
499	/** Which cell a file sits in: its placement, else the cell a plan put it in. */
500	function cellForFile(s: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, file: string): string | null {
501	  const p = s.files[file];
502	  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return cellKey(p);
503	  const planned = turn && Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file));
504	  return planned ? cellKey(planned.cell) : null;
505	}
506	
507	function fallbackCell(map: DomainMap, domain: string): string | null {
508	  const d = map.domains.find((x) => x.id === domain);
509	  const layer = d && map.layers.find((l) => l.id in d.cells);
510	  return d && layer ? cellKey({ domain, layer: layer.id }) : null;
511	}
512	
513	/**
514	 * Splits each domain edge from `edgeViews` into one segment per (source cell, target cell) pair, so a gateway
515	 * bypass to the provider (tools·logic → gateway·external) is drawn apart from calls to complete() (→ gateway·logic).
516	 * The edge's `violation` flag is kept only on the segments whose files are the violating imports.
517	 */
518	export function edgeSegments(s: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, edges: EdgeView[]): EdgeSegment[] {
519	  const map = s.map;
520	  if (!map) return [];
521	  const out: EdgeSegment[] = [];
522	  for (const e of edges) {
523	    const groups = new Map<string, { src: string; dst: string; files: ImportEdge[] }>();
524	    for (const f of e.files.length ? e.files : [{ from: '', to: '' }]) {
525	      const src = (f.from && cellForFile(s, turn, f.from)) || fallbackCell(map, e.from);
526	      const dst = (f.to && cellForFile(s, turn, f.to)) || fallbackCell(map, e.to);
527	      if (!src || !dst) continue;
528	      const k = `${src}=>${dst}`;
529	      const g = groups.get(k) ?? { src, dst, files: [] };
530	      if (f.from) g.files.push(f);
531	      groups.set(k, g);
532	    }
533	    const list: Violation[] = e.state === 'ghost' ? turn?.planViolations ?? [] : s.violations;
534	    const added = turn?.edgesAdded ?? [];
535	    for (const [pair, g] of groups) {
536	      const violation = e.violation && (groups.size === 1 || g.files.some((f) => list.some((v) => v.file === f.from && (!v.target || v.target === f.to))));
537	      const edgeKey = `${e.from}->${e.to}`;
538	      // `new` is per domain pair in edgeViews; only the cell pairs whose imports were added this turn draw in as new.
539	      const state = e.state === 'new' && !g.files.some((f) => added.some((a) => a.edge.from === f.from && a.edge.to === f.to)) ? 'existing' : e.state;
540	      out.push({ key: `${state}:${pair}`, edgeKey, pair, from: e.from, to: e.to, src: g.src, dst: g.dst, state, violation, steps: e.steps, files: g.files });
541	    }
542	  }
543	  // Existing edges first, then new, then ghosts: lanes are assigned in this order and stay stable as a turn adds edges.
544	  const rank = { existing: 0, new: 1, ghost: 2 } as const;
545	  return out.sort((a, b) => rank[a.state] - rank[b.state] || a.key.localeCompare(b.key));
546	}

550	/** Alternating lane offsets around a gutter's center: 0, +s, −s, +2s, … */
551	const lane = (i: number, s: number) => (i === 0 ? 0 : (i % 2 ? 1 : -1) * Math.ceil(i / 2) * s);

553	export type RoutedSegment = EdgeSegment & { d: string; length: number };

555	/** Orthogonal routes through the gutters, with a separate lane per segment in every gutter it uses. */
556	export function routeEdges(L: GridLayout, segs: EdgeSegment[]): RoutedSegment[] {
557	  const used = new Map<string, number>();
558	  const take = (k: string) => {
559	    const n = used.get(k) ?? 0;
560	    used.set(k, n + 1);
561	    return n;
